title: Management and Leadership for Supervisors
summary: A ten-module programme giving new and developing managers in supervisory authorities the practical skills to lead teams and make sound decisions.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors moving into management, and managers in supervisory authorities, with the practical skills to lead teams, manage performance, communicate with influence and make sound decisions under pressure.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give new and developing managers in supervisory authorities the practical management and leadership skills that technical expertise alone does not provide. Participants leave able to delegate and manage performance, build and coach high-performing teams, influence senior stakeholders, lead change and sustain their own and their team's resilience.
sections.What It Covers: The move from supervisor to manager, delegation and performance management, building high-performing teams, coaching and feedback, influencing and stakeholder communication, presenting to senior management, managing change, wellbeing and resilience, decision-making under pressure, and leading the supervisory team.
Intended Audience: Supervisors newly promoted, or preparing for promotion, into team leader and manager roles
Managers and heads of department in supervisory authorities seeking to strengthen their leadership
Technical specialists who lead projects, thematic reviews or cross-functional teams
Learning Objectives: Explain how the role changes from expert supervisor to manager and leader
Apply delegation, prioritisation and performance management techniques
Build team trust and capability through coaching and constructive feedback
Influence and communicate with senior management and external stakeholders
Lead teams through change while protecting wellbeing and resilience
Make and communicate sound decisions under pressure and agree a personal leadership plan
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions spread over several months. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, self-assessment and skills practice, and can be selected or tailored to the authority's leadership framework.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience in a supervisory or technical role is helpful. No prior management training is required.
Core Reading: Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
Patrick Lencioni, The Five Dysfunctions of a Team (2002)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)

modules.title: From Supervisor to Manager
modules.summary: The shift from being the technical expert to achieving results through others, the new expectations of a manager, and how to establish credibility with former peers.
objectives: Explain how the manager role differs from the expert supervisor role
Assess personal strengths and development needs as a manager
Establish credibility and clear expectations with a new team
syllabus: From doing to enabling: what changes on promotion
Management versus leadership in a supervisory authority
Managing former peers and setting expectations
Self-assessment: management style and development priorities

modules.title: Delegation, Prioritisation and Managing Performance
modules.summary: How to prioritise competing supervisory demands, delegate with clarity and accountability, set objectives and manage performance, including underperformance.
objectives: Apply prioritisation techniques to competing team demands
Delegate work with clear outcomes, authority and checkpoints
Manage performance and address underperformance fairly and early
syllabus: Prioritisation tools for a risk-based supervisory workload
Effective delegation: what, to whom and how much
Setting objectives and holding performance conversations
Handling underperformance and difficult people issues

modules.title: Building High-Performing Teams
modules.summary: The behavioural foundations of high-performing teams: trust, psychological safety, constructive conflict and shared ownership, and the routines that sustain them.
objectives: Explain the conditions that enable teams to perform well
Use cognitive diversity and constructive conflict to improve decisions
Design team routines that build cohesion and shared ownership
syllabus: Trust and psychological safety in supervisory teams
Constructive conflict and collaborative decision-making
Team structures, roles and routines
Building a team charter

modules.title: Coaching, Feedback and Developing Others
modules.summary: How to use coaching conversations and timely, specific feedback to develop supervisors' judgement and capability, and to build a strong feedback culture in the team.
objectives: Apply a structured coaching model in everyday management
Give feedback that is specific, balanced and actionable
Plan the development of team members' supervisory skills
syllabus: Coaching models and powerful questions
Giving and receiving feedback, including upward feedback
Developing judgement: reviewing work without rewriting it
Skills practice: a coaching conversation

modules.title: Influencing and Stakeholder Communication
modules.summary: How to map stakeholders inside and outside the authority, adapt communication style, negotiate and persuade with structured reasoning, and build productive working relationships.
objectives: Map and prioritise internal and external stakeholders
Adapt communication and influencing style to the audience
Apply structured reasoning to negotiate and persuade
syllabus: Stakeholder mapping: colleagues, senior management, firms and peer authorities
Influencing without authority
Negotiation and persuasion using structured reasoning
Communicating with emotional intelligence

modules.title: Presenting to Senior Management
modules.summary: How to prepare papers and presentations for senior management and decision-making committees that lead with the message, frame the decision and handle questions with confidence.
objectives: Structure a paper or presentation around the decision required
Deliver key messages with clarity, brevity and confidence
Handle challenging questions from senior decision-makers
syllabus: Writing for decision: the one-page summary and recommendation
Structuring a presentation: message first, evidence second
Presence, delivery and managing nerves
Skills practice: a short briefing to a senior panel

modules.title: Managing Change
modules.summary: How to lead a team through organisational change, new supervisory approaches or technology, understand reactions to change and keep the team focused and engaged.
objectives: Explain how people respond to change and why change initiatives fail
Communicate the case for change and involve the team
Plan and sustain the implementation of change in the team
syllabus: Why change happens in supervisory authorities
Reactions to change and managing resistance
Communicating and involving the team in change
Embedding change: quick wins, feedback and follow-through

modules.title: Wellbeing, Resilience and Sustainable Performance
modules.summary: The particular pressures of supervisory work, including high-profile casework and public scrutiny, and how managers protect their own and their team's wellbeing and resilience.
objectives: Explain the specific pressures of supervisory roles
Recognise early warning signs of stress and burnout in self and others
Apply practical techniques to build personal and team resilience
syllabus: Sources of pressure: workload, scrutiny and high-profile cases
Warning signs and when to intervene or seek support
Workload design and the manager's role in wellbeing
A personal and team resilience plan

modules.title: Decision-Making Under Pressure
modules.summary: How managers make and communicate sound decisions when time is short and information incomplete, recognise bias in themselves and the team, and own the outcome.
objectives: Apply structured decision-making techniques under time pressure
Recognise individual and group biases in management decisions
Communicate decisions and their rationale clearly to the team
syllabus: Process-based thinking and structured decision-making
Bias, groupthink and stress effects on judgement
Deciding with incomplete information: options, trade-offs and reversibility
Simulation: a time-pressured supervisory management decision

modules.title: Leading the Supervisory Team: Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a personal leadership plan, covering leadership style, accountability, setting direction for the team and continuing development.
objectives: Articulate a clear direction and purpose for the team
Reflect on leadership style, accountability and emotional intelligence
Produce a personal leadership development plan
syllabus: Setting direction: linking team goals to the authority's objectives
Leading with accountability and integrity
Continuing development: mentoring, coaching and peer learning
Workshop: the twelve-month personal leadership plan

related.title: Regulatory Leadership and Strategy
related.summary: An eight-module programme for the authority's leaders on mandate, governance, independence, risk appetite, growth objectives, effectiveness and leading change.

related.title: Applied AI for Supervisory Staff
related.summary: An eight-module hands-on programme helping supervisory staff use generative AI and analytics tools safely and productively in everyday supervisory work.

related.title: Core Professional Skills for Regulatory Staff
related.summary: An eight-module practical programme building the core writing, analysis, meeting, challenge, presentation and data skills that regulatory staff need every day.

related.title: Investigative and Interviewing Skills for Supervisors
related.summary: An eight-module practical programme on planning and conducting supervisory interviews and turning interview evidence into sound findings.

related.title: Supervisory Judgement and Professional Practice
related.summary: A ten-module programme on forming, documenting and defending supervisory judgements, and turning them into clear findings, letters and interventions.
